prompts: Photosynthesis is the process by which

scenes.narration: Hi, I'm Mohammed Alibhai. For Track one of the Global Innovation Build Challenge, I trained a language model from scratch. The cap is fifty million parameters, and mine has just under that. It learned from random weights on twenty billion tokens of openly licensed English text, with my own tokenizer, on one H one hundred in about eight hours.

slide.title: A 49.8M-parameter language model, trained from scratch

bullets: 49,822,228 trainable parameters, under the 50M cap
20B tokens of openly licensed English text
Our own 32,768-entry byte-level BPE tokenizer
One H100, about 8 hours per main run
No pretrained weights, no intentionally synthetic data

scenes.narration: So, the model. It's a fourteen-layer transformer, five hundred and twelve wide, with grouped-query attention, rotary embeddings, Q-K norm, and a squared ReLU. U-net style skips connect early layers to late ones, and a value residual lets every layer reuse the first layer's values. The thirty-two-thousand-entry embedding is shared with the output head and takes a third of the budget. Counted once, as one tensor, the total is forty-nine point eight million. Counted twice, it's sixty-six point six million. I report both.

bullets: Pre-norm decoder, RMSNorm, no biases
GQA: 8 query heads, 4 KV heads, dim 64
RoPE + QK-norm
MLP 512 to 1536 to 512, ReLU²
U-net skips: layer i feeds layer 13 − i
Value residual (ResFormer), 13 learned λ
Logit softcap 15, context 1,024

columns.note: 177,772 under the cap on the counted-once convention. Both conventions are reported in the README.

scenes.narration: Next, training. I used the modded nano-GPT speedrun recipe. Muon (MEW-on) updates the block matrices, and Adam W handles the embedding and scalars. The learning rate warms up, holds, then decays to zero over the last thirty-five percent, when the data switches to higher-quality sources. Averaging the last few snapshots made no difference, so I report the final weights. Near the end, both runs stopped when I hit my cloud spending limit. They resumed exactly from their last checkpoint, optimizer, random state and data position included.

bullets: Muon (lr 0.02, Nesterov 0.95) on the 84 block matrices; AdamW (lr 3e-3) on embedding and scalars
Warmup 1%, constant, then linear decay to 0 over the last 35%
524,288 tokens per step: 38,146 steps for 20B tokens
Quality anneal: at decay start, switch to FineWeb-Edu int_score ≥ 4, FineMath, Wikipedia
Checkpoint averaging (last 4 snapshots) tried: no gain, final weights reported
bf16 autocast, torch.compile, single GPU, exact resume

scenes.narration: On to the data: FineWeb-Edu, D-C-L-M, FineMath, FinePDFs and Wikipedia, all openly licensed, none of it intentionally synthetic. WikiText one-oh-three comes from Wikipedia, which is copied all over the web. Before filtering, about five percent of its test thirteen-grams turned up in our training sample. So we drop every document sharing a thirteen-gram with WikiText validation or test, just under five thousand, plus sixteen Wikipedia articles by title. The multiple-choice benchmarks aren't filtered, but the measured overlap is a handful of items.

columns.note: 4,969 documents dropped for sharing a 13-gram with WikiText-103 validation or test, plus 16 Wikipedia articles by title.
Benchmark 13-gram overlap, measured against a 300M-token sample of the filtered training shards. Benchmarks are measured, not filtered.

scenes.narration: Before spending eight GPU hours on a main run, we ran twelve one-billion-token experiments, each changing one thing. Muon beat Adam W by a wide margin. The value residual gave the biggest perplexity gain, fifty-seven down to fifty-four, for thirteen extra parameters, so I kept it. The quality anneal raised ARC-Easy but lowered PIQA (PIE-kah), so my two main runs try two strengths. With one seed each, gaps under two points are noise, so I leaned on perplexity.

slide.title: 12 arms, one change each, one seed

columns.note: WikiText-103 test word perplexity, stride 512. One seed per arm: benchmark gaps under ~2 points are noise.

scenes.narration: These are the submitted model's final numbers, after all twenty billion tokens. HellaSwag, about thirty-two percent. ARC-Easy, about fifty-five. PIQA, about sixty-two. WinoGrande, about fifty-two, close to chance. WikiText perplexity, about thirty-nine. Against the one-billion-token run, ARC-Easy is up eight points, and perplexity fell from sixty-one to thirty-nine. The PIQA drop from the strong anneal didn't show up at twenty billion, so I submitted that run. All zero-shot, on the full evaluation sets, with the L-M evaluation harness.

blocks.note: Zero-shot, full evaluation sets, lm-evaluation-harness 0.4.13. Weights: {{WEIGHTS}}. Chance is 25% on HellaSwag and 50% on WinoGrande.

scenes.narration: And now the model itself, running locally on my laptop. I give it three prompts and let it continue. It's grammatical and keeps the tone of the prompt. It also gets facts wrong and repeats itself, and in my other samples it couldn't do a simple apples word problem. That's what I'd expect at fifty million parameters.

Finally, everything needed to reproduce this is in the repository. U-V installs the pinned environment, and the Modal scripts build the data, train and evaluate. On AI use: I built this with Claude Code agents under my direction. The agents wrote the code, ran the experiments and drafted the docs. I set the goals, made the decisions, reviewed the work and paid for compute, and I can explain the code and design choices. Thanks for watching.
